title: call-outcome.v1
description: One record per call a caller-side generator placed, written once when the generator is done with the call, whatever path it took. It states what the caller observed; it never judges it. The classifier compares it with the treatment catalog. Times are Unix epoch milliseconds. ADR-0049.

run.description: The run id the runner gave the generator.

source.description: The producer: `sipp`, `loadgen`, or a product's generator name.

stream.description: The load stream the call belongs to, as the run profile names it. The same value is the `stream` label of the generator's series.

shape.description: The treatment catalog shape id the call requested.

call_id.description: The Call-ID of the caller's INVITE as sent.

started_at_ms.description: When the caller's first INVITE left the generator.

first_provisional_at_ms.description: When the first provisional response past 100 Trying (101 to 199) to the INVITE arrived: a 100 is the next hop's own acknowledgement (RFC 3261 §8.2.6.1). Null when none did.

setup_ended_at_ms.description: When the INVITE's final response arrived, or when the generator's setup deadline passed with none. Null only when the generator stopped the call before either (`ending: failed`).

answered_at_ms.description: When the 2xx to the INVITE arrived. Null when the call was never answered.

ended_at_ms.description: When the generator finished with the call and wrote this record.

phase_reached.description: The furthest point of the call: `invited` (no response), `provisional` (1xx), `answered` (2xx and ACK), `released` (the teardown completed).

early_media.description: An 18x with a session description arrived before the final.

final_code.description: The status code of the INVITE's final response. Null when none arrived.

reason.description: The failure key. With a final: the first value of its Reason header normalised to `<protocol>;cause=<n>` with the protocol lowercased (`q.850;cause=34`, `sip;cause=503`), or the status code alone (`486`) when it has no readable first value with a cause; the reason phrase is never used. Without a final: `timeout` (no final before the setup deadline), `transport` (a send or receive failed at the socket) or `protocol` (the generator stopped the call on a message it could not accept). Null on an answered call.

retry_after_s.description: The delta-seconds of the final's Retry-After header (0 when its value does not read); null or absent when the final carried none or the call had no final. Tells a refusal that asks the caller to retry later from a bare one of the same code.

ending.description: How the call ended, from the caller's facts alone: `answered` (answered, then released by the planned teardown), `rejected` (a non-2xx final), `abandoned` (the caller CANCELed by design and got the 487), `timeout` (no final by the setup deadline), `cut` (answered, then ended before the planned teardown: a BYE the caller did not expect, or a 481 to an in-dialog request or to the BYE), `stranded` (answered, and the teardown never completed: the BYE got no final), `failed` (the generator stopped the call on a protocol or transport error; see `failures`).

failures.description: Every failure the generator saw on the call, in order, each with its instant.

legs.description: The callee-side legs a generator playing both sides saw, by the role the treatment catalog names. Absent when the generator plays the caller only. A catalog leg that never opened is absent from the list.

producer_verdict.description: The generator's own class of the call (a SIPp exit label, a loadgen result class or accepted branch), kept for analysis. The classifier never reads it.

ext.description: Product fields, under the product's own key. Upstream readers ignore it; a product's impact class may read it.

at_ms.description: When the failure was seen: the response or message that failed, or the deadline that passed.

kind.description: `dialog_request`: an in-dialog request (re-INVITE, UPDATE, INFO, OPTIONS, REFER, NOTIFY, PRACK, BYE) got a non-2xx final or none. `protocol`: an unexpected or malformed message, or an RFC check finding. `transport`: a send or receive error at the socket. `generator`: the generator itself failed (a panic); not a system-under-test impact.

method.description: The request method concerned, when there is one.

code.description: The status code received, when there is one.

detail.description: A short bounded text: the RFC rule id, the step that failed, the message received.

ending.description: How the leg ended, from the callee side, in the caller's `ending` vocabulary. `rejected` is a non-2xx final the leg sent.

early_media.description: The leg sent an 18x with a session description before its final.

received.description: The in-dialog requests the leg received (ACK and CANCEL aside), a retransmission once, the first 8: what each said, for a treatment whose leg opens only after an in-dialog consult (treatment-catalog.v1 `after_consult`).

subscription_state.description: The `Subscription-State` value's state token (RFC 6665 §8.2.3), lower case.

body_hex.description: The body's first 64 bytes, in lower-case hex.
